::: {#exm-chronic-concavity}
#### Checking that the chronic medical conditions estimates are a maximum

To confirm that the estimates in @exm-chronic-mle maximize the log-likelihood,
differentiate the score components once more,
using $\partial \mu_i / \partial \beta_0 = \mu_i$
and $\partial \mu_i / \partial \beta_1 = x_i \mu_i$
([chain rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-derivatives.html#thm-chain-rule) applied to $\mu_i = e^{\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i}$):

$$
\ba
\frac{\partial^2 \llik}{\partial \beta_0^2}
&= -\sum_{i=1}^{49} \mu_i
\\
\frac{\partial^2 \llik}{\partial \beta_0 \, \partial \beta_1}
&= -\sum_{i=1}^{49} x_i \mu_i
\\
\frac{\partial^2 \llik}{\partial \beta_1^2}
&= -\sum_{i=1}^{49} x_i^2 \mu_i
\ea
$$

Writing $\vx_i \eqdef \tp{(1, x_i)}$ and $\vb \eqdef \tp{(\beta_0, \beta_1)}$,
these three second derivatives are the entries of the [Hessian matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/vector-calculus.html#def-hessian)

$$
\underbrace{\hessf{\vb}}_{2 \times 2}
= -\sum_{i=1}^{49} \mu_i
\underbrace{\vx_i}_{2 \times 1}
\underbrace{\tp{\vx_i}}_{1 \times 2},
\quad \text{since} \quad
\underbrace{\vx_i}_{2 \times 1}
\underbrace{\tp{\vx_i}}_{1 \times 2}
= \underbrace{\pmat{1 & x_i \\ x_i & x_i^2}}_{2 \times 2}.
$$

For any nonzero vector $\underbrace{\vec{a}}_{2 \times 1}$,
$\tp{\vec{a}} \hessf{\vb} \vec{a} = -\sum_{i=1}^{49} \mu_i \paren{\tp{\vec{a}} \vx_i}^2 < 0$,
because every $\mu_i > 0$
and both groups contain women
(so $\tp{\vec{a}} \vx_i \neq 0$ for some $i$).
The log-likelihood is therefore [strictly concave](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/optimization.html#def-strictly-convex),
and the [stationary point](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/optimization.html#def-stationary-point) we found is its unique maximum.
:::
